findings.summary: The percent-decoding and decoded-value checks are unreachable policy for the current filename grammar.
findings.consequence: The boundary looks like it handles encoded traversal and decoded unsafe characters, but the regex on the preceding line rejects every percent sign, slash, backslash, control, surrogate, and dot-only filename before decoding runs. That adds audit surface without observable protection.
findings.evidence: Line 178 requires SAFE_STATIC_FILENAME, which is ASCII alnum followed only by ASCII alnum, dot, underscore, or hyphen. With that precondition, fullyDecode(value) on line 179 cannot change the string, and the decoded checks on lines 180-186 duplicate facts already guaranteed by the regex.
findings.recommendation: Either simplify the function to the actual current policy, `return typeof value === "string" && SAFE_STATIC_FILENAME.test(value)`, or if encoded static filenames are intended, relax the regex to admit percent-encoded octets and keep the decoded traversal checks as the enforcing policy.
